context:
Patient: 67M with 6 wk epigastric/LUQ pain, drenching night sweats and 8 kg weight loss; ECOG 2, T2DM on metformin, taking ibuprofen 400 mg QID. PET-CT: 9.4 cm retroperitoneal/mesenteric mass plus FDG-avid R kidney, L adrenal and liver lesions; GCB DLBCL (MYC 20%, BCL2 30%, FISH negative), marrow negative, LDH 1,290, uric acid 10.4, creatinine 1.1 -> 1.5.
What this case tests: Kidney, adrenal and liver lesions are extranodal organ disease, so stage IV, IPI 5/5 and CNS-IPI 6/6. | MYC 20% / BCL2 30% with negative FISH: neither double-expressor nor double-hit, so no intensified regimen such as DA-EPOCH-R. | ECOG 2 is disease-related in a patient who wants cure: full-dose Pola-R-CHP (or R-CHOP) x6 after a steroid prephase, not mini-CHOP or palliation. | Uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN and rising creatinine mean high TLS risk: IV hydration, rasburicase after G6PD check, TLS labs every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours, stop NSAIDs. | High CNS risk: MRI brain and LP with CSF cytology/flow now; HD-MTX only as an individualized option once renal function recovers and NSAIDs are stopped.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, germinal-center B-cell type by Hans algorithm (CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1/IRF4 negative), newly diagnosed and untreated. Source: CT-guided core biopsy of the retroperitoneal mass collected 2026-09-10, final 2026-09-12, FISH addendum 2026-09-16. MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements are not detected, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma (double/triple-hit). Ki-67 about 70%; CD5, CD30, cyclin D1 and EBER negative. Bone marrow 2026-09-11 without lymphoma. The chart code C83.30 (unspecified site) can be refined to a multi-site code; this is coding only.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IV, Lugano stage IV B, with bulky disease. Basis: FDG-PET-CT 2026-09-05 shows a 9.4 x 6.8 cm retroperitoneal and mesenteric nodal conglomerate encasing the aorta and IVC without occlusion, plus FDG-avid right renal (3.2 cm), left adrenal (2.6 cm) and hepatic segment VI (1.8 cm) lesions. The liver lesion is separate from the nodal mass, so the disease is stage IV regardless of whether the renal and adrenal lesions are contiguous with nodes. B symptoms are present: drenching night sweats most nights and unintentional weight loss of about 11% (79 kg to 70.2 kg over about 2 months). Fever of 37.9 C does not meet the 38.0 C threshold and is not counted. No supradiaphragmatic FDG-avid disease. Bone marrow negative. Testes normal on exam and PET. The 4 mm right upper lobe nodule is indeterminate and does not change stage.
answer.biology: GCB-type DLBCL with high proliferation (Ki-67 70%). MYC IHC 20% (below the 40% double-expressor threshold) and BCL2 IHC 30% (below the 50% threshold), so not double-expressor by standard cut-offs; FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements, so there is no double-hit biology. EBV (EBER) negative. CD20 positive, so rituximab is indicated. TP53 status and other genotype (MYD88, CD79B, EZH2) were not reported. These would refine prognosis and trial eligibility but would not change standard first-line therapy; send them on block A1 if tissue allows.
answer.prognosis: High risk. International Prognostic Index 5 of 5: age over 60 (1), ECOG 2 (1), stage IV (1), LDH above ULN (1; 1120 U/L on 2026-09-03 and 1290 U/L on 2026-09-16, ULN 225, so about 5 to 6 times ULN and rising), and more than one extranodal site (1). Further adverse features: bulky disease, B symptoms, beta-2-microglobulin 4.8 mg/L, albumin 3.1 g/dL, hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL, rising creatinine, and rising LDH and urate over 2 weeks. Favourable features: GCB type, no MYC/BCL2/BCL6 rearrangement, negative marrow, normal LVEF (60%), CD20 positive, no CNS symptoms, HBV immune. With R-CHOP-class therapy I would expect long-term remission in roughly half to two-thirds of patients in this IPI group; quote the institutional estimates for the patient conversation. In POLARIX, polatuzumab with R-CHP improved 2-year progression-free survival over R-CHOP (about 77% vs 70%), with benefit across the higher-IPI subgroups. The rapid LDH rise and creatinine trend show biologically active disease, so the main prognostic lever now is starting therapy within days.
answer.first_line_treatment: Start curative-intent immunochemotherapy now. Target cycle 1 day 1 within about 7 days of tumor board, after the pre-treatment safety steps below are in place; do not wait for every item in missing_information. Regimen: pola-R-CHP (polatuzumab vedotin, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone) every 21 days for 6 cycles, the POLARIX schedule. Reasons: IPI 5 falls in the POLARIX population (IPI 2 to 5), NCCN lists pola-R-CHP as a preferred first-line regimen for DLBCL, it improved PFS over R-CHOP, and it omits vincristine, which matters with diabetes and the neuropathy risk. Dose full (no upfront reduction) for ECOG 2 and eGFR 50; none of these agents needs a renal dose adjustment at this level, but re-check if eGFR falls below about 30. Give primary G-CSF support (pegfilgrastim or on-body injector) for age, ECOG 2, comorbidity and the anthracycline. Cycle 1 requires inpatient or day-hospital monitoring for tumor lysis (see supportive_care). Intrathecal methotrexate CNS prophylaxis with the cycles, if he agrees after counseling (see cns_risk); avoid high-dose methotrexate given eGFR 50 and age. Fallback if polatuzumab cannot be obtained or approved: R-CHOP-21 for 6 cycles with the same supportive measures; R-CHOP-14 is less favoured because its schedule puts the cycle 6 nadir in the wedding window. Not indicated now: DA-EPOCH-R (no double-hit biology) and upfront autologous transplant. Consolidative radiotherapy to the residual retroperitoneal mass (about 30 Gy) only if still PET-avid at end of treatment. If ECOG is confirmed at 3 before cycle 1, I would switch to a dose-reduced regimen (R-mini-CHOP type) rather than full pola-R-CHP.
answer.cns_risk: High. CNS-IPI points I count: age over 60 (1), Ann Arbor stage III/IV (1), LDH above ULN (1), and renal and/or adrenal involvement (1). Four points places him in the high-risk group; ECOG and extranodal count do not change that. Check the exact point thresholds on the calculator, but he is high-risk under any version, with historical CNS relapse risk of roughly 10% or more without prophylaxis. Plan: (a) before cycle 1, brain MRI with and without gadolinium (a group II agent is acceptable at eGFR 50) and lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry, after coagulation studies. Do the LP and MRI only if they will not delay cycle 1 by more than a few days. (b) If CNS disease is excluded and he agrees after counseling, intrathecal methotrexate prophylaxis with the cycles per institutional protocol (commonly 4 to 6 doses). The evidence is observational, but it is the usual approach for high-risk patients. (c) Avoid high-dose methotrexate: eGFR 50, age, and the hydration needs of tumor lysis. (d) Neurological review at every visit; any headache, confusion, visual change, cranial nerve or focal finding prompts urgent MRI and LP. His neurological exam is currently non-focal and symptom review is negative.
answer.response_assessment: Baseline: FDG-PET-CT 2026-09-05 (nodal conglomerate SUVmax 24.1; right kidney 19.6; left adrenal 17.2; liver 15.0; liver background SUVmax 2.9) plus the 9.4 x 6.8 cm nodal dimension on CT. Record the same lesion measurements and LDH at each response assessment, and track urate and creatinine during cycle 1. Interim FDG-PET-CT after cycle 2, scored by Deauville 5-point. Deauville 1 to 3: continue the planned six cycles. Deauville 4 to 5: do not switch regimen automatically. Re-biopsy the most avid site if feasible, discuss at tumor board, and consider a clinical trial. End-of-treatment PET-CT about 3 to 4 weeks after cycle 6. Complete metabolic response (Deauville 1 to 3, no new lesions) means observation. Residual Deauville 4 to 5 at end of treatment: biopsy if clinically suspicious, and consider consolidative radiotherapy to the bulky retroperitoneal site. Renal, adrenal and hepatic lesions must resolve on imaging, not only on PET. Surveillance after complete response: clinical review every 3 to 6 months for 2 years, then less often; LDH at each visit for 2 years; imaging only for symptoms or new signs. Rising LDH, new B symptoms, or a rising creatinine that suggests obstruction as nodes shrink prompt early imaging. This is early-stage progression data, not a replacement for the scheduled PET.
answer.pretreatment_workup: Must be in place before cycle 1: (1) G6PD activity, required before rasburicase; if deficient, use allopurinol and avoid dapsone. (2) Daily urate, LDH, phosphate, potassium, calcium and creatinine through the first 72 hours of cycle 1. (3) Urinalysis with microscopy and urine protein, and renal ultrasound to exclude collecting-system obstruction from the retroperitoneal mass; creatinine has risen from 1.1 mg/dL (2025-07) to 1.5 mg/dL (2026-09-16) with eGFR 72 falling to 50, accelerating since ibuprofen was started. (4) Coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) and platelet count before LP. (5) Brain MRI and LP with CSF cytology and flow, as in cns_risk. (6) 12-lead ECG for baseline QTc before antiemetics. (7) Echocardiogram 2026-09-09: LVEF 60%, GLS -19%, grade I diastolic dysfunction. This is acceptable for an anthracycline; repeat only with symptoms. Cardiac risk factors (diabetes, hypertension, 30 pack-year smoking history) noted. (8) Hepatitis: HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive, anti-HBs reactive; no antiviral prophylaxis needed. HCV and HIV nonreactive. (9) Hepatic panel: ALP 168 U/L with normal bilirubin; add GGT to distinguish hepatic from bone source. Bilirubin 0.9 is acceptable for doxorubicin. (10) CBC with differential and reticulocyte count. (11) Baseline neuropathy exam, given diabetes and the polatuzumab and vincristine decision. (12) Weight and BSA recalculated on day 1 (last weight 70.2 kg). (13) Vaccines: inactivated influenza, COVID and pneumococcal, and recombinant zoster if available, ideally 2 weeks before cycle 1, but do not delay the start for them. (14) Pharmacy and access: polatuzumab prior authorization, G-CSF supply, rasburicase or allopurinol, and intrathecal methotrexate.
answer.supportive_care: Tumor lysis (high risk: bulky 9.4 cm disease, LDH about 5 times ULN, urate 10.4 mg/dL, phosphate 4.6 mg/dL, renal involvement and rising creatinine): stop ibuprofen now. Admit or use day-hospital monitoring for cycle 1 days 1 to 3. IV hydration with caution given hypertension, with a urine output target per protocol. If G6PD is normal, give rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg IV daily per protocol because urate is already elevated. If rasburicase is not possible, use allopurinol with renal dose adjustment plus hydration. Avoid febuxostat. Recheck electrolytes and urate every 6 to 12 hours for the first 48 hours. NSAIDs: stop ibuprofen and all NSAIDs, including OTC products; he is taking 1600 mg/day with lisinopril, rising creatinine and low platelets. Hold lisinopril through the tumor lysis window and until creatinine is stable; recheck blood pressure at each visit. Hold metformin while eGFR is 50 with hydration and contrast risk; manage glucose with insulin. Avoid IV contrast unless essential and dose-adjust renally cleared drugs. Glycemia: HbA1c 7.4% and random glucose 168 mg/dL; prednisone days 1 to 5 each cycle will raise glucose; arrange basal or NPH insulin with the prednisone schedule and glucose checks through the diabetes team. Infection: primary G-CSF; no routine antibiotic prophylaxis; written fever plan. Avoid trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole because of the sulfonamide antibiotic allergy (generalized rash, 2009). If PJP prophylaxis is used for steroid pulses, use atovaquone 1500 mg daily; avoid dapsone (sulfone cross-reactivity and G6PD risk). HBV: no prophylaxis. Antiemetics: NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist, and dexamethasone or reduced dexamethasone on prednisone days; check QTc first. Anemia (hemoglobin 9.9): transfuse for symptoms or hemoglobin below 7 to 8 g/dL, with a higher threshold given cardiac risk. Platelets 145: transfuse below 10 for bleeding or procedures. Gout (urate 10.4 with two flares, no urate-lowering therapy): allopurinol once the tumor lysis window has passed, renal-dosed; prednisone covers most flares; avoid NSAIDs; colchicine only with renal dose check and no strong CYP3A4 or P-gp inhibitors. Pain: abdominal pain from bulky retroperitoneal and mesenteric disease should improve within days of chemotherapy; scheduled acetaminophen up to 3 g/day and low-dose oxycodone or hydromorphone for breakthrough pain; avoid morphine and tramadol with eGFR 50; bowel regimen; early low-dose radiotherapy as a backup for refractory pain. Watch for bowel obstruction or ischemia from mesenteric disease and for ureteric obstruction. Gastroprotection with pantoprazole while on prednisone. Cyclophosphamide: encourage oral fluids. Tamsulosin: hold on dehydrated days if orthostatic. Nutrition: albumin 3.1 and about 11% weight loss; dietitian review and oral supplements. No routine pharmacological VTE prophylaxis; IVC is encased but not occluded, so evaluate for leg swelling or limb symptoms.
answer.fitness_and_goals: Patient goals: curative treatment, and attending his granddaughter's wedding in mid-December. He is concerned about the 45-minute drive, which his wife does. His daughter lives nearby. Fitness: age 67, ECOG 2, borderline 3 (resting much of the afternoon but still independent in self-care and walking around the house). Comorbidities: type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.4%), hypertension (controlled), gout without urate-lowering therapy, hyperlipidemia, BPH, former smoker (30 pack-years, quit 2010), LVEF 60%, eGFR 50 with progressive decline, hemoglobin 9.9, albumin 3.1. Assessment: fit for curative full-dose pola-R-CHP with supportive care; not a candidate for intensified or high-dose consolidation at this point. Recommend a brief geriatric screen (for example G8) at baseline to inform tolerance planning; it should not delay treatment. Wedding planning: with a 21-day schedule and cycle 1 around 2026-09-25 (the chart's tumor board date is 2026-09-18), cycle 4 nadir falls in late November to early December and cycle 5 starts around 2026-12-18, so mid-December attendance falls in the recovery window after cycle 4 with G-CSF support. The exact date should be confirmed once cycle 1 is scheduled, and the schedule re-checked at the cycle 3 visit. Practical plan: draw labs near home where possible, use telehealth for visits that do not need examination, use an on-body G-CSF injector to avoid an extra trip, arrange transport support and caregiver education for his wife and daughter, and consider transfer of later-cycle care to a closer infusion site. Goals-of-care: curative intent, with honest discussion that cure is likely but not certain; options; neuropathy trade-off (no vincristine with pola-R-CHP); intrathecal methotrexate toxicity; advance directive and health-care proxy. Early palliative and supportive care referral for symptom management, not comfort-only care.
missing_information: G6PD activity, needed before rasburicase (and to rule out dapsone); not in the chart
Urinalysis, urine protein and renal ultrasound: obstruction and proteinuria not excluded while creatinine rose from 1.1 to 1.5 mg/dL
Coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) before LP; not reported
CNS status: no brain MRI or LP yet; CNS-IPI is high, so this decides prophylaxis
12-lead ECG and baseline QTc; not reported
Formal ECOG confirmation (2 vs 3); no geriatric assessment on record
Baseline measurements of the lesions on CT (SPD) and PET metabolic volume for later response assessment
Source of ALP 168 U/L (liver vs bone); GGT and ALP fractionation not done
Baseline diabetic neuropathy exam, needed before polatuzumab and any vincristine decision
TP53 status and other genotype (optional; not required for the regimen choice)
Insurance approval for polatuzumab and G-CSF supply
Patient decision after counseling on pola-R-CHP vs R-CHOP and on intrathecal methotrexate prophylaxis
Clinical trial options for high-IPI, CNS-high disease are not documented
Day-1 weight and volume status; current urine output
Follow-up plan for the indeterminate 4 mm right upper lobe nodule (not expected to change management)

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype.
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage IV.
The response attributes stage IV to extranodal organ involvement of the kidney, adrenal gland and liver.
The response notes B symptoms (night sweats and/or weight loss >10% or fevers).
The response assigns this patient a stage lower than IV (stage I, II or III).
The response states the lymphoma is neither double-expressor (MYC 20%, BCL2 30% below thresholds) nor double-hit (FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-expressor.
The response calculates IPI as 5 (or explicitly high-risk IPI 4-5): age >60, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, stage IV, >1 extranodal site.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 6 or high risk (4-6), counting kidney/adrenal involvement.
The response recommends curative-intent full-dose immunochemotherapy with Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP for 6 cycles.
The response names Pola-R-CHP as the preferred regimen given IPI >=2 (R-CHOP acceptable alternative).
The response recommends a steroid prephase (e.g. prednisone ~100 mg daily for 5-7 days) before cycle 1 given age >60, ECOG 2 and high tumor burden.
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R or another intensified regimen for this patient.
The response recommends a dose-reduced regimen (e.g. R-mini-CHOP) as the initial plan, despite age 67 and disease-related ECOG 2.
The response identifies a high risk of CNS relapse driven by kidney/adrenal involvement and high CNS-IPI.
The response recommends baseline CNS evaluation: contrast MRI brain and lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry.
The response discusses CNS prophylaxis (e.g. high-dose methotrexate) as an individualized option with uncertain benefit and ties its feasibility to renal function / stopping NSAIDs.
The response schedules high-dose methotrexate immediately (e.g. with cycle 1) without addressing the rising creatinine, renal involvement, or concurrent NSAID use.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response says residual Deauville 4-5 uptake at end of treatment should be biopsied if it would change management.

The response recognizes high tumor-lysis risk (uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN, rising creatinine) and orders TLS prophylaxis with IV hydration, a uric-acid-lowering agent and frequent TLS labs (every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours; daily is not frequent enough at this risk).
The response favors rasburicase (given hyperuricemia with renal impairment) and checks G6PD before giving it.
The response recommends primary G-CSF prophylaxis (e.g. pegfilgrastim) with each cycle, given age >=65.
The response stops ibuprofen/NSAIDs (nephrotoxic with rising creatinine; interacts with methotrexate) and offers alternative analgesia.
The response anticipates steroid-induced hyperglycemia in this diabetic patient (glucose monitoring / insulin plan) or adjusts metformin for falling eGFR.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed before rituximab.
The response notes the baseline LVEF of 60% permits anthracycline.
The response judges ECOG 2 as disease-related and not a reason to de-escalate curative therapy, and acknowledges the patient's goal of cure.
